about.title: Corning Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Corning residents rely on all kinds of consumer goods, farm equipment, and household products every day, and most of the time they work as expected. But when a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning label leads to serious harm, the person hurt shouldn't have to shoulder the cost alone. California's strict liability rules mean an injured person generally doesn't need to prove the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused the injury. This can apply to the company that made the product, the distributor that shipped it, or the retailer that sold it. If you or someone in your family was hurt by a defective product in Corning, keeping the item and any packaging matters. LawProactive connects you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can review what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Claims Work Differently

items.title: Strict Liability Standard
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury. This can make these claims more direct than a typical negligence case.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can each share liability for a defective product. An attorney can help identify every party connected to the product that harmed you.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective item, its packaging, and any receipts can be critical to building a claim. An attorney can advise you on how to protect that evidence right away.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, rather than proving the company acted negligently. An independent attorney can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the item exactly as it was when the injury happened, along with any packaging, manuals, or receipts. This evidence can be important for showing what went wrong. Avoid repairing or discarding it before speaking with an attorney.

items.question: I live in a small town like Corning — can I still get help?
